items.sourceTitle: Builders are betting on a bevy of new ultra-luxe condos in West Palm Beach
items.imageResolutionReason: Existing West Palm Beach waterfront skyline editorial image selected for citywide vertical-resort context.
items.rewrittenHeadline: In West Palm Beach, luxury condo now means vertical resort
items.deck: Private marinas, wine rooms, yacht access, wellness programming, branded hospitality, and record-setting penthouse pricing are becoming the new language of West Palm Beach condo development.

bodySections.heading: The story
bodySections.body: West Palm Beach’s new-construction condo market has crossed into a new phase. The city is no longer just adding luxury towers. It is adding lifestyle systems. The newest projects are competing with resort-style amenity packages: private marinas, yacht access, wine rooms, pickleball, rooftop pools, hospitality partnerships, wellness services, concierge programming, and branded residential identities. The shift is visible across South Flagler House, Shorecrest, Edgeworth, Ritz-Carlton Residences, Mandarin Oriental Residences, Olara, Alba, and the planned Banyan Tree-branded project on Hibiscus Street.

bodySections.heading: Why it matters
bodySections.body: Buyers need to evaluate amenity quality, view protection, completion timing, corridor trajectory, service model, HOA structure, parking, marina access, and resale audience.

bodySections.heading: Brooke's take
bodySections.body: The best building is not the one with the longest amenity list. It is the one where amenities, location, views, timing, and future buyer pool actually fit how someone wants to live.

items.buyerTakeaway: The best building is not the one with the longest amenity list. It is the one where amenities, location, views, timing, and future buyer pool actually fit how someone wants to live.
items.cta: Brooke Snader with the Scott Gordon Group at Douglas Elliman Palm Beach helps buyers compare West Palm Beach new-construction condos across buildings and corridors.
items.newsletterBlurb: West Palm Beach luxury condo development is shifting from nice building to vertical resort.

items.sourceTitle: This newly redeveloped West Palm Beach neighborhood is loaded with New York spirit
items.imageResolutionReason: Exact related project image selected for nora-house.
items.rewrittenHeadline: NORA is moving from restaurant buzz to residential gravity
items.deck: NORA is becoming more than a restaurant district. With hotel, rental, and luxury condo components in motion, it may become one of West Palm Beach’s most important lifestyle corridors for buyers who want walkability and neighborhood energy.

bodySections.heading: The story
bodySections.body: NORA started as a restored warehouse district with restaurants, cafés, and a deliberate sense of place. The next buyer-facing story is what comes next: hospitality, multifamily housing, and a planned luxury condominium. For buyers comparing West Palm Beach new construction, NORA sits in a different lane than waterfront towers. It is not trying to compete with South Flagler’s direct Intracoastal views or North Flagler’s resort-marina energy. Its pitch is walkability, food, design, historic warehouse texture, and daily life.

bodySections.heading: Why it matters
bodySections.body: NORA expands the buyer map beyond direct waterfront living.

bodySections.heading: Brooke's take
bodySections.body: Buyers need to compare corridors, not just buildings. A NORA buyer and a South Flagler buyer may both want West Palm Beach new construction, but they are buying completely different daily lives.

items.buyerTakeaway: Buyers need to compare corridors, not just buildings. A NORA buyer and a South Flagler buyer may both want West Palm Beach new construction, but they are buying completely different daily lives.

items.newsletterBlurb: NORA is becoming one of the key lifestyle corridors to watch in West Palm Beach.

items.sourceTitle: Porsche, Armani and Now Music Festivals? Brands Are Taking Over Miami Condos
items.rewrittenHeadline: For West Palm Beach buyers, the brand is becoming part of the building
items.deck: As West Palm Beach adds Ritz-Carlton, Mandarin Oriental, Banyan Tree, and Cipriani-linked projects to its luxury pipeline, buyers should treat the brand as a clue to service, lifestyle, resale audience, and daily experience.

bodySections.heading: The story
bodySections.body: Branded residences have become one of the defining forces in Florida luxury real estate. Miami may be the loudest version of the trend, but West Palm Beach is building its own more restrained version. A brand can shape service expectations, amenity programming, design language, wellness offerings, and the type of buyer a building is likely to attract. The question is not whether the brand sounds impressive. The question is what the brand actually changes about the way the building lives.

bodySections.heading: Why it matters
bodySections.body: Branding can affect pricing, demand, lifestyle expectations, and resale perception, but it does not solve view quality, floor plan fit, HOA costs, construction timing, or corridor risk.

bodySections.heading: Brooke's take
bodySections.body: A brand can be useful, but it is not a magic wand. Buyers should ask what the brand actually controls: service, design, food and beverage, wellness, operations, or mostly the name.

items.buyerTakeaway: A brand can be useful, but it is not a magic wand. Buyers should ask what the brand actually controls: service, design, food and beverage, wellness, operations, or mostly the name.

items.newsletterBlurb: In West Palm Beach, the real branded-residence question is not whether the name is impressive. It is what the brand changes about daily life.
